prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
Do not start a centrally acting anticholinergic (trihexyphenidyl, benztropine) for the tremor at 71: confusion and memory impairment, and urinary retention with his prostatic hyperplasia
required_recommendations: Diagnose clinically probable PD (MDS 2015): bradykinesia with decrement and right-sided rest tremor and rigidity, no absolute exclusion, no red flag; the response to levodopa may add a supportive criterion [Postuma_2015]

Start carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg, half a tablet three times daily with food, increasing over 2 to 4 weeks to one tablet three times daily (300 mg/day levodopa), and review the response after 2 to 3 months [NICE_NG71]
Measure lying and standing blood pressure during levodopa titration, since tamsulosin and amlodipine add to orthostatic falls
Advise bedroom safety for the dream enactment (protect the bed partner, remove sharp objects, pad the bedside); if treatment is needed prefer melatonin to clonazepam at 71 (sedation, falls)
Refer to physiotherapy for gait, turning and the recent near-fall, occupational therapy for dressing and fine-motor tasks, and speech and language therapy for the hypophonia [NICE_NG71]

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure, episodic confusion or encephalopathy; the nocturnal episode is dream enactment, which is characterized by video-PSG, not EEG
No inflammatory, infectious or rapidly progressive feature: CSF has no role in this typical parkinsonism
No murmur, heart failure or cardiac symptom: an echocardiogram does not inform the parkinsonism
No syncope or palpitations; the near-fall was unsteadiness on turning: rhythm monitoring is not indicated
No cardiac symptom, syncope or QT-relevant drug planned: an ECG does not inform the parkinsonism
DaT SPECT is indicated when tremor cannot be clinically separated from parkinsonism; here the clinical diagnosis is clear and the scan would not change management [NICE_NG71]

differential.key_features: Rest tremor that re-emerges at rest and is accentuated by mental calculation, no action tremor, unilateral bradykinesia with decrement and rigidity; his father's ET is a separate condition
No dopamine receptor blocker, antiemetic or antipsychotic exposure; unilateral signs
Upper-limb onset, unilateral signs, no stepwise course, and only Fazekas 1 foci without basal ganglia lacune on MRI
No orthostatic symptoms or incontinence (urinary symptoms are attributed to known BPH), no cerebellar signs, rest tremor present, normal pons and cerebellum on MRI
Full vertical eye movements, no falls (one near-fall, pull test one step), limb rather than axial rigidity, normal midbrain on MRI
Dream enactment with parkinsonism raises it, but there is no dementia (MoCA 27/30, no cognitive complaint), no fluctuations and no visual hallucinations

key_clinical_evidence: Right-sided bradykinesia with decrement, 4-5 Hz pill-rolling rest tremor with re-emergence, cogwheel rigidity at the right wrist and ankle, micrographia, hypophonia and hypomimia: MDS 2015 parkinsonism
Rest tremor is the one supportive criterion before any levodopa trial; no red flag and no absolute exclusion: clinically probable PD
One near-fall without a fall and a pull test of one step; MoCA 27/30
Dream enactment once in the past 6 months and constipation for a year: prodromal non-motor features
MRI normal for age with Fazekas 1 foci: no vascular, structural or atypical-parkinsonism features
Tamsulosin and amlodipine add orthostatic risk once levodopa is started

alternatives: Dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole): higher risk of impulse control disorders, somnolence and hallucinations after 70
MAO-B inhibitors (rasagiline 1 mg daily) for mild symptoms
contraindications: Non-selective MAO inhibitors (phenelzine, tranylcypromine) with levodopa: risk of hypertensive crisis. Not currently prescribed.
interactions: Tamsulosin (alpha-1 blocker) lowers standing blood pressure and adds to the orthostatic fall; levodopa can lower it further. Review the need for each and measure lying and standing blood pressure at each levodopa dose step.
Amlodipine lowers blood pressure and adds to the same orthostatic effect.
Naproxen with low-dose aspirin: higher risk of gastrointestinal bleeding, and naproxen may reduce the antiplatelet effect of aspirin. Acetaminophen is the safer analgesic for back pain.
warnings: Metformin: no clinically relevant interaction with levodopa.
Nausea is common at initiation; taking the dose with a small carbohydrate snack helps.
High-protein meals reduce levodopa absorption; if fluctuations develop later, separate doses from protein-rich meals.
Dopaminergic drugs can cause somnolence and sudden sleep onset: counsel about driving.
Impulse control disorders (gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping) occur mainly with dopamine agonists; ask at follow-up visits.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Classic unilateral tremor-onset parkinsonism; arm stiffness first attributed to an old rotator cuff injury and the father's ET are distractors; 1 required criterion (MRI)
key_educational_points: Parkinson disease is a clinical diagnosis: bradykinesia with rest tremor, rigidity or both (MDS 2015; postural instability is no longer a core criterion)
Asymmetry of motor involvement is a hallmark of idiopathic PD and helps distinguish it from atypical parkinsonian syndromes
Brain MRI in PD is typically normal and is obtained primarily to exclude structural causes and features of atypical parkinsonism
DaTscan confirms presynaptic dopaminergic deficit but does not distinguish PD from MSA or PSP
Levodopa remains the gold standard treatment and a robust response supports the diagnosis

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Jianjun Liu is a 71-year-old right-handed retired electrician who presents to the neurology outpatient clinic with his wife, Maria, for evaluation of a progressively worsening right hand tremor and generalized slowing of movements over the past two and a half years. He first noticed a subtle intermittent shaking of his right hand approximately two and a half years ago, initially only occurring when he was sitting at rest watching television. He initially attributed it to fatigue and did not seek medical attention. Over the following year, the tremor became more frequent and persistent, particularly noticeable at rest but temporarily subsiding when he used his hand purposefully, such as picking up a cup of coffee. His wife was the first to point out that his right hand appeared to be trembling during church services when his hands were resting on his lap. Over the past year, he has noticed a distinct slowing in his daily activities. Buttoning his shirt now takes considerably longer, and he has started using elastic-waist pants because manipulating a belt buckle has become frustrating. His handwriting has become progressively smaller, to the point where he has difficulty reading his own notes, and he has switched to using his phone for reminders instead. He reports increased stiffness in his right arm and shoulder, which he initially thought was related to his old rotator cuff injury, but the stiffness has persisted despite anti-inflammatory medication and is now also affecting his right leg. His wife has noticed that he walks more slowly and takes smaller steps than he used to, and that his right arm does not swing as much as his left when walking. He had one near-fall episode three months ago when he turned quickly in the kitchen and felt unsteady, but he caught himself on the counter and did not actually fall. He reports difficulty turning over in bed at night and feels that his movements are generally slower and more effortful throughout the day. He has noticed some constipation over the past year, requiring him to use a fiber supplement daily, and his wife mentions that he has been speaking more softly than usual, often requiring her to ask him to repeat himself. He denies any cognitive complaints, visual hallucinations, loss of consciousness, numbness, or difficulty swallowing. His sleep has been generally adequate, although his wife has mentioned occasional movements during sleep, including once when he appeared to punch the air while apparently dreaming, which occurred approximately six months ago.

neurological_exam.additional: Resting tremor present in the right hand at 4-5 Hz, 'pill-rolling' in character, intermittently present during examination, suppressible with voluntary movement, re-emerging at rest. Tremor accentuated by mental calculation (counting backward from 100 by 7s). No tremor observed in the left hand, chin, or lower extremities. Handwriting sample shows progressive micrographia. Glabellar reflex positive (non-habituating blink to repeated tapping).
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing intact bilaterally without dysmetria. Heel-to-shin testing normal. Rapid alternating movements impaired on the right (see motor exam). No intention tremor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Facial expression is mildly hypomimic with reduced blink rate bilaterally. Remainder of cranial nerve examination normal including hearing, palate elevation, tongue protrusion midline without fasciculations.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly stooped posture. Gait initiation slightly hesitant. Reduced right arm swing during ambulation. Stride length mildly shortened bilaterally, right more than left. Mild en bloc turning (requires 4-5 steps to turn 180 degrees). No festination. Tandem gait mildly impaired. Romberg negative. Pull test: one step backward recovery, no falls.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented to person, place, time, and situation. MoCA 27/30 (lost 1 point on delayed recall, 1 point on serial sevens, 1 point on letter fluency). Speech is mildly hypophonic but fluent with intact comprehension and repetition. Naming and language functions intact. No evidence of apraxia or agnosia.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild cogwheel rigidity at the right wrist, more prominent with activation maneuver (contralateral fist clenching). Subtle rigidity at the right elbow. Left upper extremity tone normal. Mild rigidity noted at the right ankle. Strength 5/5 in all extremities bilaterally. Marked bradykinesia in the right hand demonstrated by slow, decremental finger tapping and rapid alternating movements. Left hand finger tapping mildly slow but with preserved amplitude. No pronator drift.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, and patellar tendons bilaterally. Ankle reflexes 1+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, temperature and proprioception in all extremities. Vibratory sense intact except mildly reduced at both great toes.
